drafted_figures.means: For the the latest month-end position date (a month end is the last day of the month or its last business day; a date in a month still open is not one) of each portfolio that has a signed single-name limit (a business rule of type policy or limit, the type a signed limits workbook is loaded as, whose parameters name the portfolio and the dimension single_name, with max_pct), each holding's exposure over the portfolio total in percent. A holding is over the limit when its share is above max_pct. A limit whose bucket names one holding (the signed limits workbook names Harborview Semiconductor) is tested on that holding only; a bucket of any single name, or none, on every holding. A holding is exempt only when a signed office rule says so (a business rule of type policy whose parameters name the portfolio, the dimension single_name_exempt and the instrument); with no such rule on record every holding, a sovereign note included, is tested like the others, and the policy text (section 3, any single name 0 to 5 percent) names no exception. A portfolio with holdings in more than one currency has no share worked out (status says so). A breach is real when the oldest value behind it is no older than the office's stale-value days (rule stale_value_days, else 90 days, the use-case card), otherwise it is possibly stale. Cost to cure = (exposure - limit x total) / (1 - limit), the amount to sell so the name is at the limit of what is left. A holding with no asset class is flagged.
